transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Maya Ortega (Pelion CTO), Liam Brooks (ML Engineer), Nora Chen (Security), Samir Patel (Infra)

Summary:
Pelion is evaluating migrating from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated/Private. Primary drivers: cost predictability, lower latency for certain workloads, and on-prem/VPC KMS requirements for regulated customers. They run a mix of chat and embedding workloads with custom evals; concerned about eval parity (differences in tokenization/quantization), compatibility with vLLM/TGI stacks, and security controls (SOC2, KMS, SSO).

Topics:
- Current stack and usage patterns
- Latency/cost tradeoffs and Dedicated sizing
- Model compatibility and eval parity (OpenAI vs Redwood-hosted/dedicated)
- Private deployment and KMS/HSM integration
- Benchmarks + next steps

Action items (captured by attendees in call):
- Avery to send pricing + sizing options and architecture note
- Ravi to propose benchmark plan and test harness
- Maya to share representative prompts and PII examples
- Nora to request SOC2 + KMS docs from Redwood

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery with Redwood Inference, I'm the AE on the account, with me is Ravi, our solutions engineer. Quick intros?
[00:12] Maya: Hi I'm Maya, CTO at Pelion, we run the platform ML team. We've been using OpenAI for prod and want to explore Dedicated or Private to reduce cost and get more control.
[00:22] Liam: Liam here, I own model infra, we also prototype with vLLM locally and use T G I in some benches, sorry, T G I is Text Generation Inference.
[00:30] Ravi: Great, thanks. To set expectations — today we want to understand your workloads, traffic patterns, success criteria for migration, and any security constraints.
[00:39] Maya: Sure. Quick context — about 20M tokens/month currently, mix of chat assistant and embeddings for semantic search. Latency is important for chat routes, we have a 300-400ms target p50 but can tolerate higher p95. Cost is getting expensive on OpenAI at scale.
[00:54] Samir: From infra side we need VPC peering, private link or a plan for on-prem if needed. Also KMS/HSM for keys and key rotation requirements.
[01:02] Nora: Security wants SOC2, audit logs, RBAC, and confirmation that data retention policies can be configured.
[01:08] Avery: Totally — Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with VPC options, and our Private deploy supports customer-managed KMS/HSM. We have SOC2 and ISO docs we can share. For eval parity, Ravi can dig into the model compatibility and quantization concerns.
[01:22] Ravi: Yeah, quick note — when customers move from OpenAI to Dedicated, most differences come from model variant (architecture + fine-tune), tokenizer differences and quantization (gpt-style fp16 vs int8/4) which can shift probabilities. We typically run an eval harness against representative prompts and compute metrics like exact match, ROUGE, BLEU where applicable, and human evals for quality drift.
[01:45] Liam: How does Redwood handle vLLM/TGI compatibility? We have an internal stack with vLLM for local infra and some teams use T G I containers.
[01:53] Ravi: Redwood supports model variants and we can host standard open models as-is; for vLLM/TGI artifacts, runtime compatibility is mostly at model and tokenizer level. If you have a TGI repository or vLLM checkpoint, we can usually convert or load the model weights — there can be caveats around custom kernels and optimizations. We also provide recommendations on quantization profiles to hit a target latency without degrading eval metrics too much.
[02:18] Maya: The big question is eval parity. If we move off OpenAI, will the outputs be consistent enough for our downstream semantic scoring and business rules?
[02:26] Ravi: Short answer: you'll need to run your evals. We aim for parity but due to different decoders and sampling, parameters like temperature, top-p, and tokenizer differences can create variation. Our approach is to match model family and seed prompt engineering, then run side-by-side A/B with metric thresholds you define. We can help set up a benchmark run and provide tooling to compare outputs automatically.
[02:45] Nora: Also compliance: is key material kept in our KMS? We can't have Redwood manage keys for certain customers.
[02:51] Avery: For Private deployments yes, customer-managed KMS is supported. For Dedicated we offer integration with customer KMS/TLS peering and strict audit logs — we can surface detailed network diagrams and KMS integration docs in the security pack.
[03:04] Liam: On latency — we've seen OpenAI p50 around 250ms for our small prompts. Can Dedicated match that?
[03:11] Ravi: It depends on instance types and batching behavior. With Dedicated reserved GPUs we can configure lower-concurrency single-request paths and pre-warm KV cache for chat workloads; that tends to bring p50 near or under your target. We'll propose a sizing that balances throughput and latency. There is also a cost tradeoff — lower latency often needs more reserved capacity.
[03:31] Maya: What about cost modeling? We pay per token now to OpenAI; what's the typical delta on Redwood dedicated?
[03:38] Avery: For Dedicated it's usually a commit plus unit economics for GPU hours; our team will model expected tokens/throughput and show cost per 1M tokens vs current spend. We also optimize with batching and KV caching to reduce billable tokens. I'll send a sample pro forma.
[03:52] Samir: Any known issues moving fine-tuned models? We have a few model variants and a custom fine-tune for safety filters.
[04:00] Ravi: Fine-tunes can be moved; often we either host the fine-tuned variant directly or reproduce the fine-tune on the same base model in our infra. We check checkpoints and tokenizers. One gotcha: optimization passes and quantization can slightly change safety classifier sensitivity, so we recommend running safety/regression tests as part of the migration.
[04:20] Maya: Can you run an initial benchmark with our prompts and show delta vs OpenAI?
[04:25] Avery: Yes — next step would be you share 4-5 representative prompt categories and some sample inputs (scrubbed for PII if needed), Ravi will design the harness, and we'll run side-by-side tests.
[04:35] Liam: On conversion — we use vLLM with custom kernels for faster attention. Will Redwood's runtime leverage the same kernels or do you rely on different kernels that might affect perf?
[04:44] Ravi: Our runtime includes optimized kernels and a kernel selection layer — we pick the best implementation per hardware and sequence length. That means sometimes perf will be better; sometimes different. For vLLM-specific kernels there's overlap but for a few custom community kernels we may have to replicate behavior. We'll include that in the benchmark scope.
[04:59] Nora: About logs and auditing — we need detailed per-request logs for compliance, retention policy, and possibility to redact PII.
[05:06] Avery: We have request-level audit logs, token-level cost breakdowns, and you can configure retention windows. For Private deployments you can keep logs on-prem. We'll include redaction best-practices.
[05:18] Maya: Any blockers we should expect in timeline? We want to decide in ~3 weeks and run a pilot in 4-6 weeks.
[05:25] Ravi: Common blockers: detailed evaluation metric disagreements, security sign-off (SOC2/KMS), and data residency requirements. We can parallelize — while security reviews happen we run bench tests on a small sample.
[05:37] Liam: On the technical side — auth and SSO. We use SAML with Okta and need RBAC integration.
[05:42] Avery: Supported — we integrate with SAML/Okta and provide RBAC. We'll send configuration docs.
[05:48] Maya: One more — are there model variants you recommend to get closest behavior to OpenAI gpt-4 style outputs?
[05:55] Ravi: Depends on your use case. For chat parity we recommend matching model family (decoder vs encoder-decoder), and often a few tuning steps. We'll propose a shortlist of vetted open models and Redwood-verified performance profiles — that'll be in the doc package.
[06:10] Nora: For the SOC2 package, can we get the report and the network diagram?
[06:14] Avery: Yes, I'll attach the SOC2 report and a network diagram with VPC options.
[06:18] Maya: Great. Also, please call out any features that could cause differences in eval metrics — like int8 quantization or compressed KV cache.
[06:27] Ravi: We'll include quantization profiles and expected impacts. In our experience int8 can change a few percent of token-level outputs; human evals sometimes show smaller perceptual differences but we always advocate running your own thresholds.
[06:42] Liam: Regarding embeddings — we use OpenAI embeddings for semantic search. If we move, will Redwood embeddings be drop-in with same vector space?
[06:50] Ravi: Not guaranteed. Embedding spaces vary by model and training. We recommend running a regression test: index a sample corpus with both embeddings and measure retrieval metrics (MRR, recall@k). If you need exact parity, one approach is to continue using OpenAI embeddings for a period or host the exact embedding model if weights are available.
[07:10] Maya: Ok good. Let's talk logistics for benchmarks — what do you need from us?
[07:15] Ravi: Sample prompts (4-5 categories), 100-500 examples per category ideally, expected metrics you care about, and any PII rules. We'll set up harness, run side-by-side on matching model family and provide raw outputs + diffs + metric report.
[07:30] Maya: We'll try to get that by end of week.
[07:33] Avery: Perfect. I'll follow up with an email outlining next steps, attachments: pricing draft, security pack, benchmark plan.
[07:40] Nora: One more Q — do you support bringing our own model weights? We have an internal fine-tune we want to run on Dedicated.
[07:46] Ravi: Yes, BYO weights is supported in most cases; we'll validate format and suggest any conversion steps. For on-prem/private we can host them behind your network.
[07:57] Maya: That answers most of our questions. Thanks.
[08:00] Avery: Quick recap: Avery to send pricing + security pack; Ravi to scope benchmark + test harness; Pelion to share prompts and PII examples; Nora to request SOC2 docs and confirm KMS constraints. We'll aim for a bench run in ~2 weeks and a decision within 3 weeks.
[08:18] Maya: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:20] Liam: Thanks.
[08:22] Nora: Thanks.

End of call.
